title: Succession

Diesel deal unwinds —
he says get a new leader
I've seen this excuse

haiku:
One old pipe still holds
law's slow water flowing on
a judge still unbent

haiku:
Unseen, the main holds
a jurist, patient as pipe,
wins the prize at last

haiku:
Canadian words
still find the clearest channel
through old sediment

haiku:
Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught

backed up rent they can't afford
Madrid finds its voice

haiku:
Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm

He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true

the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain

no untested water flows
wisdom, for once, wins

downstream, new water

Nine votes hold the line
the crooked district unbent
water finds its grade

yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow

one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.

More days in the pipe
a valve cracked, and time flows on
I'll take the extra.

Old allies reroute
round a wall no one can name
water finds its way

One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge

someone tried to brew plague code
and the pipe held fast

Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks

old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this

missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause

keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows

title: Backflow

Court unclogs the pipe,
dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.

the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry

the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends

Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water

Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow

Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea

learns to filter what returns—
old pipes, new gasket.

Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way

I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow

Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer

Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle

The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now

title: Unthrottled

Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open

so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.

and the crude runs calm

young hands raise their phones like pipes
truth still finds its grade

Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks

and the bridge that lifts the light

a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote

a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war

bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break

brooms outlast bombers

to watch walls give up

when my students were still young —
now the olives burn

hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk

all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand

clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat

bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars

flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold

bones in the dry wash

one voice climbs the marble steps

wrote down what a person's owed—

the ocean had no vote here—

ships walk uphill now

the bottom of the whole world—

to find a pinch that glowed blue—

iron lace against gray sky,

the rest, he said, is our job

share one long and branching root—

no scream, only sleep

at one dark spot in the sky—

swung round Jupiter each night—
